checks: The affine tangent below the minimum denominator is positive there, matches the inverse-power slope at the join, and gives a convex C1 continuation. The gauge sum is continuous and coercive, the sublevel sets are nested, and the value at zero is below one for small parameter.

For every ray, the derivative of the radial equation is bounded below by the inverse outer radius minus a uniform O(epsilon) quantity. Bounded f first gives O(epsilon) displacement and Lipschitz f gives the O(epsilon^2) refinement. The radial dth-power volume expansion has first coefficient rho^d f, including the two-ray d=1 case.

The positive projective map fixes ray directions and has image radial length rho/(1+a·rho u), which identifies the coefficient as d times the image cap volume. Integration over at most the whole sphere gives the claimed common remainder.

The attained energy Jacobian and first-moment identity make the image a centroid-zero body. A containing cap includes its central parallel subcap, and removed layers are nonnegative. Projecting the first radial displacement at a regular old point gives h_K(n)f.
